title: On Improving the HLS Compatibility of Large C/C++ Code Regions
problem: HLS tools impose restrictions on supported C/C++ language features, limiting the size and variety of code regions that can be offloaded to hardware accelerators in heterogeneous CPU-FPGA applications. Non-synthesizable constructs such as dynamic memory allocation and unsupported language features prevent larger code regions from compilation.
motivation: Expanding the size and diversity of synthesizable code regions increases the applicability and performance benefits of HLS-based hardware acceleration in heterogeneous computing systems.
method: The paper proposes automated code transformations to circumvent HLS restrictions: struct and array flattening to simplify data structures, moving dynamic memory allocations outside synthesizable regions, converting dynamic allocations to static allocations determined at compile time, and asynchronously executing host-side functions such as printf() to eliminate unsynthesizable operations.
key_novelty: Systematic set of code transformation techniques that automatically improve HLS compatibility by addressing fundamental C/C++ language feature restrictions limiting synthesizable region size.
contributions: Code transformation techniques for struct/array flattening and dynamic memory relocation
Asynchronous execution strategy for unsynthesizable host functions
Evaluation demonstrating increased synthesizable code region size across three real-world applications
Practical methodology for extending HLS applicability to larger heterogeneous code segments
limitations: Evaluation limited to three applications with no detailed performance or energy measurements reported.
primary_theme: HLS compatibility improvement through code transformation
